papers.title: Initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations
papers.abstract: We study initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations on the half-line. We first give a systematic account of fundamental solutions for equations with general finite-range interactions. We then develop complementary approaches based on reflection, the Laplace transform, and the unified transform method, obtaining contour integral and Bessel-function representations of solutions. For the semidiscrete diffusion equation, we justify these representations for continuous boundary data and initial data of polynomial growth, establish uniqueness in the corresponding growth class, and derive spatial estimates and long-time properties, including asymptotic periodicity. We also treat nonhomogeneous equations, Robin boundary conditions, nonsymmetric coefficients, and a class of time-dependent coefficients. Finally, higher-order examples illustrate how the unified transform approach extends beyond second-order equations.

papers.title: A semiampleness result for hyperk\"ahler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
papers.abstract: We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperk\"ahler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.

papers.title: On global Chern-Calabi flows on compact complex surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose the Chern-Calabi Flow for extremal metrics in conformal Hermitian geometry. After the existence of extremal metric, we consider the existence of global flows to the Chern-Calabi flows for extremal metrics on compact complex surfaces with Gauduchon metrics. To achieve this goal, we use the Adams inequality and the Gronwall inequality method to obtain fourth order derivative norm estimates. We also study the convergence of the global solution to the Chern-Calabi flow and its limit is the solution of the Chern-Calabi extremal metric problem. We propose a fourth order elliptic problem and derive the Bochner formula relevant to the elliptic estimates for the Chern-Calabi heat flow.

papers.title: Continuation and convergence for the higher dimensional conformal Chern--Calabi flow
papers.abstract: We study the volume-normalized gradient flow of the squared Chern scalar curvature on compact Hermitian manifolds of complex dimension $n\ge3$. The flow extends smoothly past a finite time if the spatial supremum of Chern scalar curvature belongs to $L^2$ in time. A uniform curvature bound in the evolving $L^p$ norm, for one fixed $p>n$, gives global existence and smooth convergence of the whole trajectory to a constrained critical metric. On Chern scalar-flat backgrounds, small initial $L^p$ curvature gives exponential convergence to the background. A corresponding condition on the trace-free first Chern--Ricci form gives exponential convergence on Chern--Ricci-flat Hermitian and positive K\"ahler--Einstein backgrounds. The smallness thresholds are independent of the initial higher derivatives. We also construct constant Chern scalar curvature backgrounds of either sign with arbitrarily small smooth perturbations whose solutions, if global, cannot converge back to the background.

papers.title: Concavity-Free $L^\infty$ Estimates and Stability for Fully Nonlinear Complex Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the $L^\infty$ estimates of Guo-Phong for fully non-linear equations on compact hermitian manifolds to a possibly indefinite reference form satisfying a uniform admissibility criterion. Furthermore, we also establish one-sided stability estimates. Neither result requires homogeneity or concavity of the nonlinear operator.

papers.title: Explicit meromorphic solutions of certain types of nonlinear differential-difference equations
papers.abstract: Our main purpose is to determine all meromorphic solutions, in explicit form, of the nonlinear differential-difference equations \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+q(z)f(z+c)=p_{1}{\rm e}^{\alpha_{1}z}+p_{2}{\rm e}^{\alpha_{2}z} \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+q(z){\rm e}^{Q(z)}f(z+c)=p_{1}{\rm e}^{\alpha_{1}z}+p_{2}{\rm e}^{\alpha_{2}z}, \end{equation*} where $n\geq 3$ is an integer, $q(z)$ and $Q(z)$ are nonzero polynomials with $Q(z)$ nonconstant, and $c,~p_{j},~\alpha_{j}(j=1,2)$ are nonzero constants satisfying $\alpha_{1}\neq \alpha_{2}$. We sharpen the result in the cited literature, as illustrated by specific examples.

papers.title: Comprehensive Resolution of the Gauss-Fourier Conjecture for the First Kind of Zeros
papers.abstract: For over two centuries, the esteemed mathematicians Gauss and Fourier conjectured that each real critical point of the rational function $p^{'}(s)/p(s)$ is associated with a pair of non-real zeros of the real polynomial $p(s)$. The conjecture remains unresolved. The real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ that are real multiple zero of $p^{'}(s)$ are defined as the second kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. In addition to the second kind of zeros, the other real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ are referred to as the first kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. We demonstrate that the first kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ emerge from the intersection of root loci emitted from non-real zeros of $p(s)$, thereby providing a comprehensive geometric interpretation of their relationship. Moreover, each first kind of zero of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ is connected via root loci to a pair of conjugate non-real zeros of $p(s)$. This establishes the precise geometric relationship conjectured by Gauss and Fourier, fully resolving their original problem for first-kind zeros and completing a foundational chapter in polynomial theory. We have proven Gauss-Fourier conjecture about the first kind of zeros.

papers.title: Octonionic and Monogenic Completions of Harmonic Functions
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain, with $n\ge2$. We characterize the real-valued harmonic functions that can occur as prescribed real components of monogenic functions. For any fixed nonzero real Clifford module $M$ and any fixed unit vector $s\in M$, a smooth real-valued function $h$ can be written as $h=\langle F,s\rangle$ with $F$ monogenic if and only if the $(n-1)$-form $*dh$ is exact. Consequently, every real-valued harmonic function on $\Omega$ admits such a representation if and only if $H_{\mathrm{dR}}^{n-1}(\Omega)=0$. In dimension eight, the same exactness criterion characterizes the real parts of octonionic regular functions and yields the corresponding equivalence with $H_{\mathrm{dR}}^7(\Omega)=0$. The proofs use global solvability of the Poisson equation and elementary identities for differential forms.

papers.title: Comparison of the Bergman and Szeg\H{o} kernels on arbitrary bounded pseudoconvex domains with $C^2$ boundary
papers.abstract: On every bounded pseudoconvex domain $\Omega\Subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge2$, with $C^2$ boundary, we prove $K_\Omega/S_\Omega\le C_{\Omega,\varepsilon} \delta_\Omega^{-1}|\log\delta_\Omega|^{1+\varepsilon}$ near the boundary for every $\varepsilon>0$, where $\delta_\Omega$ denotes the boundary distance. For each positive nondecreasing $H(s)=o(s)$, a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex complete Reinhardt domain in $\mathbb C^2$ shows that the logarithmic factor cannot be replaced by $H(|\log\delta_\Omega|)$.

papers.title: The Hardy-Littlewood-type equivalence problem and its applications
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to resolve the Hardy-Littlewood-type equivalence problem. In particular, we show that a Hardy-Littlewood-type theorem holds for arbitrary majorants in the case \(p\in(1,\infty)\), and that the equivalence holds in the case \(p=1\). For the proof, we employ new functional analytic approaches based on Fourier series, the Hilbert transform, and the uniform boundedness principle. Those proof methods are completely different from those of Dyakonov [Acta Math., 178 (1997), 143-167] and Pavlovi\'c [Acta Math., 183 (1999), 141-143]. In addition, we present several representative applications that improve a series of known results.

papers.title: Bounded symbols and one-component geometry
papers.abstract: We prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on a Hardy model space admits a bounded symbol if and only if its defining inner function is one-component, meaning that it has a connected sublevel set at some level in $(0,1)$. This resolves the bounded symbol conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi and Timotin and, through known equivalences, the embedding and weak factorization conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin. A uniform bound $R$ for the ratio of least bounded symbol norm to operator norm on the rank-one family associated with point evaluation in the disk already forces this geometry. The corresponding bound for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators is at most $CR\log(e+R)$, where $C$ is absolute, and the logarithmic factor is optimal. In a nonzero de Branges space, the same geometric condition characterizes when every sufficiently small equivalent change of norm preserving the de Branges structure is represented exactly by reweighting the original integral with a positive density bounded above and away from zero. This characterization remains valid when the norm changes are restricted to discrete sampling norms. Outside the one-component class, every model space admits self-adjoint trace class truncated Toeplitz operators without bounded symbols, with arbitrarily small norm and singular values satisfying any prescribed positive upper bounds.

papers.title: Markman--Markushevich principle and Lagrangian fibrations on O'Grady six-manifolds
papers.abstract: To any compact holomorphically symplectic manifold and a nef BBF-isotropic class we associate a quasi-projective variety called the Markman--Markushevich space which parametrises the Lagrangian fibrations with this isotropic class modulo Tate--Shafarevich twists. We give a systematic interpretation of known results about Tate--Shafarevich twists of Lagrangian fibrations using this space, employ it to obtain a conjectural result for the last deformation type for which such a result is not yet proposed, and make some first steps towards its proof. As a byproduct, we generalise the results of Kumar on existence Shioda--Inose partners for abelian surfaces to a slightly more general class of K3 surfaces, and associate a canonical K3 surface with transcendental lattice isometric to $U^2\oplus\langle-2\rangle^2$ to a smooth cubic surface with a choice of a Schl\"afli double-six. Finally, we construct a noncompact six-manifold with an abelian fibration associated to a cubic surface with a Schl\"afli double-six, and give its interpretation in terms of the K3 surfaces we introduced.

papers.title: Fekete Points as Norming Sets for Random Holomorphic Sections
papers.abstract: We prove that Fekete configurations associated with a positive Hermitian line bundle over a compact K\"ahler manifold are asymptotically exact norming sets for random holomorphic sections. For every fixed $a>0$, the ratio of the supremum norm of a degree-$k$ section to its maximum on the degree-$\lceil ak\rceil$ Fekete configuration converges to one in probability. This holds for any background K\"ahler form: Fekete equidistribution provides enough sampling points near the maximum of the limiting pointwise variance. We obtain polynomial upper bounds for the tail of the ratio and almost-sure norm comparisons. In contrast, when the limiting variance is nonconstant, we construct separated arrays of cardinality comparable to the section-space dimension for which the ratio converges to a constant strictly greater than one. General separated arrays still satisfy probabilistic norming inequalities with degree-independent constants, and every such array is asymptotically exact if and only if the volume form is proportional to $c_1(L,h)^n$. We also prove a discrete $L^2$ norm comparison with exponentially small exceptional probability. The norm comparisons and convergence statements hold in both the Gaussian and spherical ensembles.

papers.title: Selberg and Brolin on value distribution of complex dynamics
papers.abstract: The Brolin-Lyubich-Freire--Lopes--Ma\~n\'e equidistribution theorem for iterated preimages of a given non-exceptional value and Lyubich's periodic point version of it are foundational in the study of dynamics of rational functions of degree more than one on the complex projective line, and Drasin and the author studied a quantification of the former in a formalism of Nevanlinna theory, or more specifically, with the aid of Selberg's theorem from covering theory. In this paper, we point out that the argument in that previous study has already yielded a better quantification of the Brolin-Lyubich-Freire--Lopes--Ma\~n\'e equidistribution theorem, and also point out that a similar argument also yields a quantification of Lyubich's theorem under an exponentwise version of the so called hypothesis H, which has recently been settled by Przytycki for unicritical polynomials. As an application, we sharpen the quantitative results on the value distribution of the (first) derivatives of iterated polynomials.

papers.title: On weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics
papers.abstract: The notion of weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics extends the classical notion of Calabi's extremal K\"ahler metrics, but includes many well-studied objects in K\"ahler geometry such as K\"ahler-Ricci solitons and Sasaki-Einstein metrics. In this paper, after explaining how this notion grew out, we will try to survey recent works concerning the YTD conjecture on weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics.

papers.title: Sharp coefficient, logarithmic and Schwarzian estimates for $\alpha$-convex functions on the real line
papers.abstract: The class $M_\alpha$ of $\alpha$-convex functions, introduced by Mocanu in 1969, interpolates between starlike ($\alpha=0$) and convex ($\alpha=1$) mappings and has traditionally been studied only for $\alpha\geq0$. We show that several of its sharp invariant estimates in fact extend to the entire real line. Our main result characterizes $M_\alpha$ for every real $\alpha\neq0$ through an explicit pointwise inequality, generalizing a theorem of Chuaqui, Duren and Osgood from the convex case, and we determine the sharp value of $\beta$ for which $M_\alpha\subset C_\beta$ when $\alpha\geq1$; we also show that the reciprocal inclusion $C_\beta\subset M_\alpha$ fails for every $\alpha>1$. Building on this, we obtain a sharp Fekete--Szeg\H{o} inequality, valid for every $\alpha\notin\{0,-1,-1/2\}$, and sharp bounds for the first two logarithmic coefficients of $M_\alpha$, which recover the classical values for starlike and convex functions as special cases. We also determine the order of $M_\alpha$, establish a piecewise sharp bound for its Schwarzian norm together with an explicit quasiconformal extension criterion via the Ahlfors--Weill theorem, and compute the Schwarzian norm of the $\alpha$-Koebe function explicitly for $\alpha=1/n$, $n\in\mathbb N$, verified for $n\leq9$ and numerically supported for $n<50$, leading to a conjecture for the general case. Finally, we propose a conjectural sharp bound for the second Hankel determinant of $M_\alpha$, consistent with the known values $1$ and $1/8$ for the starlike and convex subclasses.

papers.title: Measure rigidity for regular polynomial endomorphisms and applications
papers.abstract: We classify regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^k$ with the same equilibrium measure under some mild condition on the dynamics at infinity. In particular, for $f$ in a Zariski dense open subset of the parameter space and any $g$ of the same degree, $\mu_g=\mu_f$ if and only if $f=g$. We also establish finiteness results for maps with a prescribed equilibrium measure. Our approach rests on the stable manifold structure near the hyperplane at infinity. Applications include a Tits-type alternative, results on iterated centralizers, and an arithmetic non-density theorem.

papers.title: Asymptotic Root Dynamics under Repeated and Fractional Integration
papers.abstract: Fix a polynomial $P(x)=\sum_{j=0}^m a_jx^j$ of degree $m$, and let $I_kP$ be its $k$-fold antiderivative with all integration constants zero. Borwein, Chen, and Dilcher proved that, after $x=ky$, the nonzero zeros of $I_kP$ converge to the nonzero zeros of $L[P](y)=\sum_j a_j j! y^j$. That convergence determines the leading linear motion but neither the constant offset nor successive differences. We compute the next two terms at a simple nonzero zero $\lambda$ of $L[P]$. Integer-order and Riemann-Liouville integration reduce, after scaling, to one rational family $c_j(h)=\prod_{\ell\le j}(1+\ell h)^{-1}$ sampled at $h=1/k$ and $h=1/\alpha$. We prove $r_k=k\lambda+C_P(\lambda)+D_P(\lambda)/k+O(k^{-2})$ with explicit $C_P$ and $D_P$. Hence $\lambda$ is at once the scaled zero, the limit of successive root differences, and the continuous-order velocity, each with an explicit correction; $C_P(\lambda)$ is the offset of an asymptotic line. For binomials the limiting spacing is a multiple of a gamma-ratio quantity, the Factorial Fraction, and the nonzero reduced zeros form an exact regular polygon at every positive order. For real quadratics the collision order of two branches takes a simple discriminant form. In every degree the collision discriminant carries a universal factor, the one familiar from Laguerre polynomials and supported at negative orders. In the coordinates $(\alpha,x)$ all trajectories lie on one plane curve of degree $m$ with leading form $L[P]$. At a nonzero zero of $L[P]$ of multiplicity $q$, the nearby zeros split on the scale $\sqrt{k}$ like the zeros of the Hermite polynomial $He_q$, and for real $P$ the nonzero zeros stay real at every positive order exactly when $L[P]$ is real-rooted.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem
papers.abstract: We show that if a contractible Stein manifold $X$ with the density property admits a proper holomorphic embedding into $\mathbb{C}^k$, then $X \times \mathbb{C}^k$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+k}$ with $n=\dim X$. We also prove that McLean's exotic affine variety $K_n$, $n\ge4$, a smooth contractible affine variety which is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$, has the density property. Hence for $n \ge 4$ there exist an integer $m \in \{ n, \dots, 2n\}$ and an affine variety $X$ such that $X \times \mathbb{C}$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{m+1}$ and $X$ is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^m$. This settles the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem in the negative.
